utterances.text: Witness, you need not go into so many details on this. Was Seselj involved in the Plitvice event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the JNA intervene in Plitvice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, they did. The JNA did intervene and prevented the clash from escalating by separating the two opposing sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the Serbs stay in control in Plitvice after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you mentioned that actually on that day you had prepared for negotiations with the Croatian government. Did that take place, the negotiations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Negotiations did take place one day before that. When we went to the talks, we said that we would decide upon the negotiations, and then there was a repeated round of negotiations with the Croatian government to quieten down the situation, the whole situation around Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What happened in Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: What happened in Borovo Selo was that the Croatians started provocations, and then the Serbs shut off all the access roads to Borovo Selo. And when this happened Goran Hadzic was arrested and he was someone of great authority, who enjoyed great authority there. He was beaten up and we helped them to be freed and returned to Borovo Selo. We did this together with the Croatian authorities. And we asked that the roads, access roads to Borovo Selo be reopened, and the Serbs did do so. Several days later, the MUP of Croatia stormed the village and started shooting in the village, and there was major clash between the Serbs there and the Croatian police force and some Croatian policemen were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the JNA intervene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, it did intervene.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the Serbian people stay in control in Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What happened in July 1990 in Srb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: There was a large meeting of Serbs, and the Serb National Council was set up on the occasion. A large number of Serbs from Croatia had arrived but so had a large number of Serbs from Bosnia-Herzegovina as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were they invited there or how -- you -- first of all, were you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. present during this meeting in Srb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was present there too.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And why were the Bosnian Serbs there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Well, they wanted to show that they couldn't be separated from the Serbs in Croatia and that they wanted it to remain one state and to lend their support to the Serbs in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were politicians from Belgrade present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: There was Vojislav Seselj, but he was just passing by at the time. He didn't even deliver a speech of any kind. I didn't notice anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why was this Serb National Council founded, and what did it demand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I can't say exactly what the goal was, but I think it was something that Milan Babic forced. He wanted to make himself more important, and also to have the Serbs articulate themselves and say that they were together, that they wanted the Serb question to be solved within the composition of one state and that Croatia must become more reasonable and understand the Serb question and to have a show of force as to unity and number.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When -- was there -- when was the Association of Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika founded? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I think sometime very soon after these events, which is to say sometime at the end of 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what was the reason for founding this organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: One of the reasons was that they no longer agreed with the SDS views in Croatia and they wanted to wage an autonomous policy and in those municipalities there were like-minded people and they didn't want to have any more contacts with Croatia and created their own autonomous region with their own autonomous policies.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The Serb National Council that was founded in Srb, was it meant to cover all the Serbian territories in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No. No, it wasn't, because definition wasn't given to the areas and borders yet that that should cover.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the Serb National Council get support from Belgrade? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was a similar institution founded for Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes. The Serb National Council of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem was formed later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: It was formed at the beginning or, rather, the end of 1990 and at the beginning of 1991 at the latest. I'm not sure of the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Western Slavonia part of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No, it was not part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: We didn't have our representatives there. Nobody discussed it with us. We didn't take part in it and, therefore, we considered that we were not a part of that. Perhaps they assumed that we ought to be, but they didn't actually discuss the matter ever with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to put an exhibit to the witness, and it's actually Exhibit C124, and which -- is it a tab?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We need to get these exhibits into order. We've got here what is described as an exhibit bundle for Witness 037. Now, is it going to be convenient if we treat that in the way we've treated the exhibits put through witnesses, a large number, that is, before? Namely, to gave the entire bundle a witness -- an exhibit number and then refer to tabs thereafter?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's actually prepared this way. But I wouldn't know which tab this is now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Yes. Well, we'll give the bundle, first of all, an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 327.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: For the moment, we'll have to refer to it as tab 124, I think, or --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's tab 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tab 2. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think in the binder the exhibits are listed according to how I use them. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- you can follow this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, I can follow but it's a matter of how it goes in the record which is important so that we can refer to it hereafter. Very well. When we get to these exhibits, perhaps the registrar will tell us the tab numbers so we have a formal record of it. This one is tab 2. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, this is a letter of the Serbian National Council of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, dated the 28th of May, 1991, to the Federal Presidency in Belgrade. It is signed by a person, Ilija Petrovic. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, I do know the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who was he? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Well, at the time, he was in that National Council of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. I don't know what post he held exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you aware that such a letter went to the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Looking at the middle paragraph in this letter, where it says that, "Serbs are left defenceless to Croatian state terror." Do you have this line?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's in the translation in the second paragraph in the first third.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were the citizens in Western Slavonia subjected to state terror?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: At that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And a little bit further in the same paragraph, it says that: "All the police stations in Croatia dispose or work with classified lists of Serbs who allegedly participated in armed mutiny and should be arrested or killed." Is that true? Was that so in Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I don't think so, because nobody was arrested then nor were they liquidated.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in the last paragraph, it refers to the threat to the survival of the Serb nation. Was the Serb nation under threat of survival in Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This witness, Croatia 37, is being asked to comment on a letter by the Serb National Council of Eastern Slavonia where he himself spoke of the violence and killings in Borovo Selo and so on and so forth, and yet he's being asked whether anything like that happened in Western Slavonia in order to deny what is said about Eastern Slavonia. I think this is highly improper and that it is your duty to warn counsel about this improper examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness can answer questions about matters which he knows. If he doesn't know the answer, he can give it. As for the weight of the evidence, that's something you can cross-examine about and we'll have to determine at the end. But at the moment if there are matters within his knowledge, such as events in Slavonia at the time, he can give them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The letter refers to Eastern, not to Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We hear the point you make. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like to enter this into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can take it that unless there's objection raised, that the entire bundle is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. I would like -- this is dealt with now. I would like to put another letter from that same body to the witness, and it is Exhibit C182, and it should be at tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you see that it is a -- another letter of that same Ilija Petrovic to, the Federal Presidency from the 4th of August, 1991, and there is the first sentence in there, where it says: "The council does not accept any and nobody's offer for the creation of political and cultural autonomy of Serbian people in Croatia." And my question is: Was such an offer made at that time, before the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: There were proposals on the Croatian side that the question of the autonomy of Serbs in Croatia should be resolved.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And was it -- was it agreed upon by people or rejected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: This offer was rejected. There were no talks with Knin or Eastern Slavonia. Nobody discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the question to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned Goran Hadzic. Where did he live at that time and what was his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: He lived in Vukovar. He was the vice-president and deputy president of the Regional Board of the SDS, and later on he was a member of the Serb National Council for Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Srem, but I don't know what his function there was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Later on, what further functions, if any, did he have in the later years? Can you tell us which position he had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: First of all, he was the president of the SAO of Eastern Slavonia or, rather, Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem; and later on, he was the president of the republic, RSK.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you meet him personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you describe his personality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Well, he was not a serious person. He liked to live a comfortable life. He was not an extremist to begin with. After his arrest in Plitvice, he became more and more extreme, but he was always mostly concerned with himself and his own way of life.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say he was not a serious person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: He was never prepared to take things seriously. He behaved in a superficial manner; carelessly, irresponsibly.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he -- you mentioned his position that he had. Did he have leadership skills?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No. No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Given his positions, how, then, could he perform them? How could he be the president of the RSK or the president of the SAO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: He became the president of the RSK as a substitute for Babic, and attempts were made or, rather, he was put in place of Babic because of the Vance-Owen Plan. There was nobody else who had more political authority than he did because he was always being pushed forward into the limelight. But I think that he was not up to the job, that he was not really up to what was required of him at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said he was pushed into the limelight. By whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: First of all, by the people at the local level; and later on, he had support in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you say "later on," what time period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period when the RSK was being set up and when he was appointed president of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who supported him from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I can say that Budimir Kosutic did. He helped with the staffing. I don't know who he contacted about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Budimir Kosutic, which position did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: He was then I think the vice-president or Deputy Prime Minister of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You described Mr. Hadzic as a person who did not take things serious. Was he the decision-maker in the SAO Slavonia and later in the RSK?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: He was the one who put forward the decisions in public. But when they were made, I don't know who he consulted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: While there was this Serb National Council in the Krajina and the Serb National Council for Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, which approach did Western Slavonia take in 1991 -- in 1999 [sic] and 1991? Did you also form a sort of forum or a sort of council?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No. Later on, we established the SAO of Western Slavonia in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you continue, in 1991, to negotiate with the Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes. I had contacts throughout 1991, up until the outbreak of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the SDS in Western Slavonia arm the local Serbs and the Serb -- and did they establish Serb TO forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: The SDS did not provide weapons, but some people who perhaps were in the SDS perhaps did that, the party itself didn't do it. But later on, the Serbs set up Territorial Defence defence units in the municipalities in Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When did they do it and when did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I noticed that after the 19th of August, but it started probably from the beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: When the war broke out, I saw the Territorial Defence staffs had been set up, that people had weapons, that there were commands. And I know that this cannot be organised in one day or half a day.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned already earlier that there was a referendum, and I would like to talk to you -- with you about this. The first referendum of the Serb people, when did it take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: The first was in 1990 and was in favour of the cultural autonomy of the Serbs in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And who initiated this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: The SDS of Croatia did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What were the results of this referendum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Most of the Serbs voted in favour of cultural autonomy in Croatia. This was a desire to draw attention to the position of the Serbs and to have it discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This second referendum -- sorry. Was there a second referendum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes. A second referendum was held on the 12th of May, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was it about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: This referendum was the Serbs saying whether they wanted to remain in Yugoslavia, because on the 19th of May, Croatia said it wanted to secede from Yugoslavia. The Serbs wanted to express their desire to remain within Yugoslavia. However, Babic also had the idea that annexation to Serbia should be added to the referendum. Most Serbs and most people in the SDS were not in favour of this wording, so the wording was actually that the Serbs wanted to remain within Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the help of the usher, I would like to put the Exhibit 2278 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, this is a report on a meeting of the Regional SDS Board held on 8th May, 1991. Did the Regional SDS Board meet on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did it meet in the village Smrtici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On this document, there is an agenda for this meeting. Do you recall this agenda and these items on the agenda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No, I don't. There was a referendum but not as an item on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. agenda. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This document, have you -- are these the minutes of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you usually take minutes, and if so, how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Minutes were taken by the secretary of the Regional Board, and then he would put it in the archives.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On -- in the last line before the completion hour, there is a person mentioned with the name Zeljko Mandic. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: He was a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he sometimes attend meetings of the SDS board?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I didn't notice him there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were the meetings of the board, were they sometimes or always public?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to go now into private session again because this exhibit needs to be discussed in more detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a matter that has arisen that leads me to ask for a couple of minutes in closed session, if Your Honours would be good enough. I wouldn't do it if it wasn't urgent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Closed session for two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're now in open session. Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's come to our attention that there may be efforts to identify and to publish identification of this witness not by direct means but by some other slightly more subtle means. Any means of identifying protected witnesses, in our submission, would be a serious contempt of this Tribunal and would lead to the appropriate sanctions being taken or imposed on editors who take such a course of action, and we would invite the Chamber to remind editors of their duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We make it plain that any form of identification of a witness by a newspaper, or indeed any other broadcast or other outlet, is a contempt of this Tribunal. The purpose of these protective measures is to protect the witnesses, and for good reason. They're not made lightly. Therefore, any attempt by whatever means to identify a witness does amount to a contempt and will be the subject of sanctions. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the SDS leadership in Croatia have contacts with the SPS in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I do not know about any contacts that a leader like Jovan Raskovic had. As for Milan Babic and the others, I cannot say with certainty that they had any contacts, but they said that they had contacts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: They said that themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When did they say that? Did they say that publicly or when did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: They said that at meetings of the main board in Knin during 1990, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did they say or indicate with whom they had these contacts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have already mentioned that on this meeting in Srb, there were Serbs from Bosnia. Did you know whether the SDS leadership in Croatia had contacts with the SDS leadership in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who had contacts with whom, and how do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: At first these were contacts between Karadzic and Raskovic, and later these were contacts between Babic and Karadzic. They themselves said that they were going to these meetings. So Raskovic spoke about this and Milan Babic spoke about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you put it into a time frame? When did they have contacts? Can you say which years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Well, it was in 1990 and in 1991. That is to say already in 1990, towards the end of 1990, and the beginning of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in relation to the contacts with SPS Serbia, when would such contacts take place? When did you hear of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: There were contacts at the end of 1990 when a delegation representing the Serbs in Croatia went to call on President Jovic and Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to go into private session now because we come to meetings which are very particular and very specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Are we in -- yes, open.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned an association of Serbs in Croatia. What kind of association was this and who were the members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: The association consisted of Serbs who were originally from Croatia and they were living and working in Serbia. Some of them were elderly people. Some were retirees. Some were army officers. Their positions were pretty hard-line. I know that after the session with Mr. Milosevic, they attacked me, that the Serb Sparta should not be attacked. Knin was the Serb Sparta for them and they did not have any understanding for everything that was going on later in Western Slavonia. They gave more support to Milan Babic. They did not give support to Jovan Raskovic. Some of them actually wanted Jovan Raskovic to be replaced so that only Milan Babic would be the leader of the Serb Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This association, did it have contacts with the official Belgrade, in particular, Mr. Milosevic? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: They said that they had contacts, but I never saw that. I did not have any clearer knowledge with regard to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were statements and declarations of this organisation published in the Belgrade media or were they rather unknown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they were. They were published. Not that often, but they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know a person with the name Boro Rasua?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who was he and what position did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Well, it was my understanding that he originally came from Knin, and he was one of the advisors to Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know a person Brana Cuncevic or Cumetic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Crncevic. I know him. He was a writer. He probably still is one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he support the more radical Serbs in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes. He supported the more radical stream in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did they have -- did both, I mean Barane or Boro Rasua, did they have contacts with Mr. Milosevic or officials, higher officials --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, we really are getting some way from what the witness can say, I suspect. If you want to establish this evidence - and at the moment I'm not sure of the relevance of it - we must establish on what basis the witness knows what he's going to talk about.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to ask him that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, do that first of all.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know whether these people had contacts with Milosevic or the Belgrade authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: As for Boro Rasua, I don't know for sure. Perhaps he did, I don't know. As for Brana Crncevic, I haven't got any indicators showing that he would have been with Mr. Milosevic. I heard that he was close to him, but that's just something I heard. I couldn't say for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You have already mentioned Mr. Kosutic being involved in Eastern Slavonia. Did he also have discussions with the Serbs in Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. May. The witness did not say Budimir Kosutic -- he is a professor at Belgrade University, by the way -- he did not say he was involved in the events in Slavonia. The witness spoke about contacts of persons because he also originally came from those areas. He talked about contacts. He did not talk about involvement. So the question cannot phrased that way, speaking of involvement, because he had not said that Kosutic had been involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, I think you should rephrase it, and also we need to know what the relevance of all this is.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Kosutic was the vice minister of Serbia and I think when he has contacts with the Serbs in Croatia, it is of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. But let's ask the witness rather than discussing it generally. Can you assist us, Witness 037, as to this, whether there were contacts? Do you know of it of your own knowledge or, again, is it something which you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kosutic came to Western Slavonia at the invitation of our colleagues who had been his students. He came to help us in formulating our amendments to the proposed constitution of the Republic of Croatia according to which the Serbs were supposed to be a minority. We as a political party wanted then to make an amendment professionally, in an expert manner. At that time, Mr. Kosutic was only a university professor. Later on, I think it was the end of 1991, the second half of 1991 - I don't know exactly - he became Deputy Prime Minister, but it is afterwards that he became Deputy Prime Minister. And we did have contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he approve of your course of negotiations with the Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: He did not. Later, notably everything that was going on in Western Slavonia, he thought that we were not taking the right course. He personally objected that we talk to Franjo Tudjman and that we maintain contacts with that government. He thought that that was a non-democratic government and that one should not negotiate with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have already mentioned that some of the Serbs -- Serb leaders in the Krajina had contacts with the Bosnian Serbs. Did Milan Martic actually fight, assist them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Milan Martic took part in penetrating the -- with the corridor in Bosanska Posavina. He enjoyed quite a reputation there because of these military successes, and he became famous and indeed got authority among the Bosnian Serbs. He helped them acquire this corridor, and this was a lifesaver because there weren't enough medicines at that time. And also the region of Banja Luka and, therefore, Krajina, could not meet many of their medical needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you happen to know where he fought in the Posavina Corridor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Well, he was somewhere in the area of Doboj. I think towards Orasje, as far as I heard from people who were with him. They said that they were in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And at what time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I think this was the end of May, beginning of June 1992. That's my assessment. I can't really say the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he promoted for taking part in this fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: He got the rank of general from the president of the republic, Goran Hadzic, as recognition.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like now to address an intercepted conversation, and for this purpose we would need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, when did the -- when was the SAO Krajina founded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: It was founded at the end of 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And who was the president?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: The president was Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he in control of the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the SAO Krajina have a government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Well, he promoted that, that they had a government, but I wasn't able to see their ministries at all to see how they were functioning. All I heard was that it was a government of sorts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know who was the -- was there a JNA present in Knin, in the region of this SAO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, there was a barracks in Knin, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander in this region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When was the SAO Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: It was founded at the beginning of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And who was the president?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the Exhibit C647.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 7 -- excuse me; tab 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, it is -- item 647 is a decision of the appointment of the SAO government of the 25th of September, 1991. When you look at paragraph Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. III here, is that the government of the SAO Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, that that was that particular government meeting of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But do you have -- looking at the persons listed in paragraph III, do you know that they had these positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes. I know about Goran Hadzic, and I know about Vojin Susa. I know about Slavko Dokmanovic, Ilija Petrovic, Milan Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We do not need to go through all these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is the only question I have. I would also like to have the witness look at the Exhibit 558.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 3 -- excuse me; tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I would like you to look at the stamp of this decision on the dismissal of the secretary of the Vukovar Secretariat of Interior on the stamp and on the signature.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Are they genuine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: That's what it looked like. The stamps and the signature looked that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you happen to know what was the background, why the chief of police of Vukovar was dismissed? Do you happen to know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I don't know that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like now the witness to have a look at the Exhibit C2322.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It is the decision on the election of the carriers of the legal functions from the 9th of October, 1991, and when you look at this decision, there is mentioning of the District Court of Vukovar with temporary offices in Dalj, at various sections of this decision.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you know whether these -- whether there was this special -- this -- not special, temporary office of the District Court or higher courts in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you look at the persons elected in various positions here, either at the courts or at the prosecutor's office, are some of them familiar to you? Could you verify that this is a genuine document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I know some of the names. I recognise some of them, and they really were judges. And at least judging by the ones I know, I know that they were judges. I recognise some of the names. I know them.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you know whether the -- Ilija Koncarevic who was mentioned here as the president, was he the president of the Great National Assembly of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This is enough with the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Speaking of Mr. Hadzic, was he in control of the police of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, the SAO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Well, I think he was. I haven't got any arguments to bear that out, but I am able to conclude this because they were all like-minded persons, people that thought the same way.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know who was in control of the TO in the region of SAO Western Slavonia -- of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No. I can't know that because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know a person Radovan Stojicic, nicknamed Badza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No. I just heard about him from the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Arkan present in the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Arkan present in the SAO Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, he was present. I saw him in the course of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we need to go into private session, because I would have to ask the witness about his circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I was saying, the war was getting closer to Western Slavonia. It was in full throes. And it was our wish that it should not envelope Western Slavonia and would be considered as an area under Krajina and Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. So the SAO of Western Slavonia was formed so as to endeavour to make contacts with Zagreb and the authorities in Croatia to seek a peaceful solution and avoid a clash and conflict at all cost.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Until August 1991, did you still have a mixed police force in Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was it financed by the Ministry of Interior of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What about the police in Pakrac? Did that also apply to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: It applied to them too, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In relation to the local government employees in Western Slavonia, were they also financed by the Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What about the staff in the Secretariat for National Defence in Western Slavonia? Were they paid by the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When the SAO Western Slavonia was declared, did you at the same time also establish the government and government institutions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: There was no government or any institutions or any separate offices or anything like that. It was just something that they were working towards.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were such institutions ever established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Well, actually it wasn't a goal of any kind to set up government or institutions, just a political body for negotiations to try and avoid a war and to distance ourselves from what was happening in Western Slavonia and so that nothing should be placed in the context of the war events.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What about Jovo Vezmar? We have already mentioned him now. Did he agree to this or did he do otherwise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: No, he didn't agree with that. He formed the TO in Pakrac and waged war.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the time period from August 1991 until February 1992 when the RSK was founded, who paid, who financed the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Well, up until the end of October, I don't think anybody did. At least, not to my knowledge. Later on, I heard from people who were within the TO that they did receive salaries through the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what about the police? Who financed the police from August of -- from the outbreak of the war, from August 1991 to February 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I think that that was the police -- that the police received salaries that way later on, from October onwards, because it came under the organisation of the TO as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you say it was financed this way, you mean through the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: From which organ or which institution of the JNA? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move now to the section territories and crimes that happened on these territories, but I see it's a quarter to two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which paragraph is that, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It is paragraph 62 onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume there, then, on Monday. Witness C-037, could you be back, please, on Monday morning at 9.00, when we will resume your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 30th day of September, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
